chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the woman who menstruates while she is in a state of janabah — is a ghusl for janabah required of her? He said: The ghusl for janabah and the menstruation (haydh) is one.

key_terms.جَنَابَة: janabah — the state of major ritual impurity arising from sexual intercourse or ejaculation, requiring ghusl (ritual bath) before prayer
key_terms.جُنُب: junub — a person in the state of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.حَيْض: haydh — menstruation; the period of monthly bleeding in women, during which certain acts of worship (such as prayer and fasting) are prohibited
key_terms.غُسْل: ghusl — the obligatory full-body ritual bath required to remove major ritual impurity (janabah, haydh, etc.)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman who is menstruating and also in a state of janabah need to perform two separate ghusls according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the jurisprudential question of whether a woman who is simultaneously in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity from sexual intercourse) and haydh (menstruation) must perform two separate ritual baths (ghusls). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a single ghusl suffices for both states of impurity, establishing an important principle of consolidation in Islamic ritual law. This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that one act of purification can satisfy multiple concurrent ritual obligations.
word_analysis: in a state of sexual impurity (janabah)

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the woman who menstruates and she is with sexual impurity. Is there a major ablution (from sexual impurity) upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘The major ablution (for sexual impurity) and (for) the menstruation (Haydh), is one’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a woman who experiences Hayd (menses) when she has had sexual relation if she needed Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relation.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Ghusl (bath) for Hayd (menses) and sexual relation is one.’”
